title: Wait for a page condition
description: Wait, bounded, for one condition on the page instead of polling dsagent.page.observe: the revision to change (sinceRevision), a target to appear or go (targetId + expectedRevision), text to show, the address to change, the page to settle, a surface to close (surfaceId from pageSurfaces), the…
guidance: Wait, bounded, for one condition on the page instead of polling dsagent.page.observe: the revision to change (sinceRevision), a target to appear or go (targetId + expectedRevision), text to show, the address to change, the page to settle, a surface to close (surfaceId from pageSurfaces), the sign-in wall to clear, or a file the page saves to finish downloading. Returns met or timed-out with the latest revision; then observe with baseRevision. Read-only: no idempotency key, nothing is dispatched. Use it after an action whose receipt said pageSettled false, after a navigation the page performs itself, while the person signs in (authentication-cleared), or before acting on a panel that is still opening. A timed-out wait is not a failure of the page: read it and decide. A page the browser is not drawing is refused with PAGE_NOT_RENDERED before waiting: dsagent.page.focus, then wait again.

inputSchema.description: The page, the condition and its bound.

pageContextId.description: Opaque page context from dsagent.pages.list, dsagent.page.open, or a receipt's destinationPageContextId.

until.description: revision-changed: the page revision differs from sinceRevision. target-present / target-absent: the target (targetId at expectedRevision, from the latest observation) is visible / gone. text-present: the page shows the text (labels or visible text). url-changed: the address differs from the one at the start of the wait. settled: the page went quiet (no control-relevant mutations, its own requests finished). surface-closed: the surface with surfaceId is no longer open. authentication-cleared: the sign-in or verification wall is gone. download: a file the page started saving since your latest action on it (or since the wait began) finished downloading, or the browser stopped it (download.state says which); use it after a click whose page saves the file later: an export it builds first, a "your download will start" countdown, a document the server renders.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait at most; 10000 by default.

sinceRevision.description: With revision-changed: the revision you hold.

targetId.description: With target-present / target-absent: the opaque target.

expectedRevision.description: With targetId: the revision it was published at.

text.description: With text-present: the words the page should show, as it prints them.

surfaceId.description: With surface-closed: the surface from pageSurfaces.

outputSchema.description: Whether the condition was met within the bound, and where the page is now.

pageContextId.description: Opaque page context from dsagent.pages.list, dsagent.page.open, or a receipt's destinationPageContextId.

outcome.description: met: the condition held; timed-out: it did not within timeoutMs (read the page and decide; it is not an error).

revision.description: The page revision when the wait ended (a met wait reads the page again if its condition did not), current enough to act at; pass it as baseRevision to the next observe.

url.description: The page address as last read.

change.description: With sinceRevision: whether the latest revision differs from it.

authentication.description: With authentication-cleared and timed-out: the wall still standing (status, kind).

download.description: With download, once the page started one: the file as the browser saved it. A timed-out wait with state in_progress: the file is still arriving; wait again rather than clicking again.

state.description: complete: saved in the Downloads folder; in_progress: still arriving; interrupted: the browser stopped it (a server error, a refused or cancelled download): the file was not saved.

fileName.description: The name it was saved under, with the numbering the browser gives duplicates; never a folder.

sizeBytes.description: Its size in bytes (the bytes announced while it is still arriving).

mimeType.description: The type the server sent it as.

interruptReason.description: With interrupted: why the browser stopped it (SERVER_BAD_CONTENT, NETWORK_FAILED, USER_CANCELED...).
